subject: Civil Engineering
title: Movable Bridges: Bridges That Open
description: Learn Movable Bridges: Bridges That Open in one minute.

hook.text: Ships need to pass and the bridge is in the way. So the bridge moves.

buildup.text: Bascule bridges tilt upward. Swing bridges rotate. Lift bridges rise straight up.

discovery.text: Tower Bridge in London is a bascule — its two halves tilt up in under a minute.

twist.text: Moving bridges need massive counterweights to balance the deck during opening.

climax.text: Chicago has more movable bridges than any city — over 40 across its river.

punchline.text: When the road can't go over, the bridge makes way.

quiz.question: What type of movable bridge does Tower Bridge in London use?
options: Vertical lift — the deck rises straight up between towers
Bascule — the two halves tilt upward on pivots
Swing — the bridge rotates horizontally on a center pier

details.summary: Movable bridges open to allow vessel passage through waterways and include bascule bridges that tilt upward, swing bridges that rotate horizontally, and vertical lift bridges that raise the entire deck.
details.whyItMatters: Movable bridges solve the conflict between road transportation and waterway navigation. They are essential in port cities and along inland waterways where fixed bridges would block shipping.
takeaways: Bascule bridges tilt upward like a drawbridge using counterweights
Swing bridges rotate horizontally around a central pier
Vertical lift bridges raise the entire deck between two towers

faq.question: Which type of movable bridge is most common today?
faq.answer: Bascule bridges are most common because they open quickly, provide unlimited vertical clearance when open, and their counterweight systems require relatively modest operating power. Tower Bridge in London and many modern port city bridges use the bascule principle.

faq.question: What are the main maintenance challenges for movable bridges?
faq.answer: The mechanical components including gears, bearings, motors, and counterweight systems require constant maintenance. Salt water and weather exposure accelerate corrosion of moving parts. Electrical and control systems must function reliably to avoid stranding traffic or blocking navigation.
